- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overpredicts downward trend; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is volatile (±0.5 or more in last 5 days).
